topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The opening frames the lecture within the cancer course and states what students should learn about cancer causation.

topics.label: Mutation and clonal evolution in cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how mutations arise and enable susceptible cells to evolve into cancer within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Assessing environmental contributions to cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence that environmental exposures contribute to cancer rather than attributing its occurrence solely to chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infection can drive cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a detailed example of cooperating infectious influences.

topics.label: Mechanisms of environmentally induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how environmental exposures become mutagenic through processes that damage DNA and disrupt its accurate replication.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish why mutational initiation may require subsequent promotion that supports the growth of altered cells.

topics.label: Context-dependent susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the biological context of exposure determines susceptibility to carcinogens and consolidate the preceding mechanisms of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methods for investigating carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how evidence can identify carcinogenic exposures and assess their effects despite the limitations of available investigative methods.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: The closing draws together the lecture’s conclusions about environmental cancer risks and their assessment in everyday risk–benefit decisions.
